title: Do You Know Where the Word OK Comes From?
summary: The word OK began as a joke abbreviation in a newspaper almost 200 years ago. Here is how a silly spelling joke became an everyday word.

beats.text: You say OK every day. But what do those two letters stand for? Pause and guess!
Here's a clue: it was born in a city newspaper, almost two hundred years ago.
Back then, writers loved funny abbreviations of deliberately misspelled words.
Time's up. Where did OK come from?
beats.reveal: A joke! It stood for "oll korrect", a playful misspelling of "all correct".

beats.text: The joke was catchy. People kept using it, and the meaning stayed the same.
Bonus: most of the other joke abbreviations from that time are long forgotten.

visual.text: Most joke abbreviations of that time vanished. OK is the one that survived.
